items.title: B-spline spaces and knot conventions
items.statement: For a finite nondecreasing clamped knot vector on a bounded interval and degree p, recursively define the B-splines, their multiplicities and the piecewise-polynomial spline space; the accompanying theorem establishes their support, continuity, partition, and basis properties.

references.title: Tom Lyche, Carla Manni, and Hendrik Speleers, B-Splines and Spline Approximation, CIME 2017, §§1.1–1.2 and §2.2, PDF pp. 2–15, 25–29

items.title: Natural cubic splines
items.statement: On a bounded interval [a,b] and at distinct ordered knots t_1<...<t_r, r>=2, a natural cubic spline is a C^2 function that is polynomial of degree at most three between successive knots, has second derivative zero at the extreme knots, and is extended linearly on data-free end intervals.

references.title: Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Splines and RKHS Methods, Berkeley, Spring 2023, §§2.1–2.4, PDF pp. 3–6

items.title: Bounded local spline quasi-interpolants
items.statement: A local quasi-interpolant is a linear map from continuous L^q functions into the spline space that depends only on bounded local neighborhoods, reproduces P_l, and satisfies a mesh-uniform cellwise L^q stability bound.

references.title: Tom Lyche, Carla Manni, and Hendrik Speleers, B-Splines and Spline Approximation, CIME 2017, §§1.1–1.2 and §2.2, PDF pp. 2–15, 25–29

items.title: Natural cubic smoothing spline
items.statement: For lambda>0 and data with at least two distinct inputs in [a,b], the natural cubic smoothing spline is the minimizer of the squared empirical residual plus lambda times the integrated squared second derivative over W^{2,2}(a,b), using the continuous Sobolev representative.

references.title: Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Splines and RKHS Methods, Berkeley, Spring 2023, §§2.1–2.4, PDF pp. 3–6

items.title: Natural cubic interpolation at distinct knots
items.statement: At r at least 2 strictly increasing knots and arbitrary real values there is a unique natural cubic interpolant, linear outside the extreme knots; its interior nodal second derivatives solve a positive-definite tridiagonal system.

references.title: Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Splines and RKHS Methods, Berkeley, Spring 2023, §§2.1–2.4, PDF pp. 3–6

items.title: B-spline basis properties and polynomial reproduction
items.statement: For a finite clamped knot vector, the recursively defined degree-p B-splines form a basis of the piecewise-polynomial space with continuity p-m at a knot of multiplicity m, and reproduce every polynomial of degree at most p.

references.title: Tom Lyche, Carla Manni, and Hendrik Speleers, B-Splines and Spline Approximation, CIME 2017, §§1.1–1.2 and §2.2, PDF pp. 2–15, 25–29

items.title: Series least squares with a spline basis
items.statement: Given a fixed B-spline design vector and observed data, the series least-squares fit is the projection of the response vector onto the design column space; its defined target is the fitted training vector and its loss is squared empirical prediction error.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT OCW 14.385, Fall 2007, Proposition 3 and proof, PDF pp. 10–11

items.title: Existence, uniqueness, and spline reduction for cubic smoothing
items.statement: With lambda>0 and at least two distinct input locations, the variational problem defining the natural cubic smoothing spline has a unique minimizer; it is a natural cubic spline with knots at the distinct inputs and linear tails.

references.title: Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Splines and RKHS Methods, Berkeley, Spring 2023, §§2.1–2.4, PDF pp. 3–6

items.title: Sobolev approximation by local spline quasi-interpolants
items.statement: For 0<=l<=p, 1<=q<=infinity, f in W^{l+1,q}, and a bounded local quasi-interpolant reproducing P_l, local and global L^q errors are bounded by a constant times the (l+1)-st power of the controlled local mesh size times ||D^{l+1}f||_q; on uniform meshes the cellwise L^2 projector supplies the q=2 spline rate.

references.title: Tom Lyche, Carla Manni, and Hendrik Speleers, B-Splines and Spline Approximation, CIME 2017, §§1.1–1.2 and §2.2, PDF pp. 2–15, 25–29

items.title: Expected empirical training risk for spline series least squares
items.statement: For iid real-valued pairs with a supplied Borel conditional-law kernel, a supplied Borel conditional mean with finite conditional first absolute moment, conditional variance at most Delta, and L^2(P_X) spline approximation error at most C^2K^{-2gamma}, expected empirical training-vector loss is at most Delta K/n+C^2K^{-2gamma}.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT OCW 14.385, Fall 2007, Proposition 3 and proof, PDF pp. 10–11

items.title: Sobolev rate for spline-series training risk
items.statement: For a univariate W^{s,2} regression target on a compact interval supporting the design law with bounded density, degree p>=s-1 and a uniform full-multiplicity knot mesh of dimension K=(p+1)J, expected empirical training-vector risk is O(n^{-2s/(2s+1)}) when J is comparable to n^{1/(2s+1)}.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT OCW 14.385, Fall 2007, Proposition 3 and proof, PDF pp. 10–11

items.title: One observation does not determine a natural cubic smoothing fit
items.statement: If the cubic smoothing objective is extended to a single distinct input, every affine function through that input has zero residual and zero roughness, so the minimizing function is not unique.

references.title: Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Splines and RKHS Methods, Berkeley, Spring 2023, §§2.1–2.4, PDF pp. 3–6

items.title: A quadratic Bernstein B-spline basis
items.statement: On [0,1], the clamped degree-two knot vector gives the Bernstein basis; the three functions are nonnegative, sum to one, and reproduce every quadratic polynomial.

references.title: Tom Lyche, Carla Manni, and Hendrik Speleers, B-Splines and Spline Approximation, CIME 2017, §§1.1–1.2 and §2.2, PDF pp. 2–15, 25–29

items.title: Natural cubic interpolation with two and three knots
items.statement: Two distinct knots give their unique linear interpolant; for three equally spaced knots with values 0,1,0, the middle nodal second derivative is -3 and the two cubic pieces are explicit.

references.title: Ryan Tibshirani, Nonparametric Regression: Splines and RKHS Methods, Berkeley, Spring 2023, §§2.1–2.4, PDF pp. 3–6

items.title: Uniform-mesh linear spline approximation
items.statement: For a W^{2,infinity} function, linear interpolation on a uniform knot mesh is a bounded local quasi-interpolant reproducing affine functions and has uniform error at most h^2 times the essential supremum of the second weak derivative divided by 8.

references.title: Tom Lyche, Carla Manni, and Hendrik Speleers, B-Splines and Spline Approximation, CIME 2017, §§1.1–1.2 and §2.2, PDF pp. 2–15, 25–29

items.title: Training risk and independent test risk are different quantities
items.statement: On a one-row degree-one clamped B-spline design, the fit can have zero empirical training loss while its squared error under an independent uniform test draw is 1/3.

references.title: Whitney K. Newey, Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation, MIT OCW 14.385, Fall 2007, Proposition 3 and proof, PDF pp. 10–11
